stable.label: scratch-environment-ci-pass
stable.note: The clean scratch engine now includes a cave/atmosphere/multi-fluid environment layer with fresh Codehood and Foundation CI evidence. Deployed browser/iPhone behavior after this change is still unverified.

active_experience.runtime: vanilla JavaScript modules + Worker + transferred OffscreenCanvas; no third-party runtime libraries
simulation_changes: the existing deterministic terrain, surface shallow-water, erosion, plants and ALife organism loop remain active
a persistent 2D environmental cell volume now represents underground solid/void topology instead of the surface heightfield pretending to contain caves
deterministic cave chambers and shafts are carved into that cell volume below the surface
cave cells carry oxygen, carbon dioxide, water vapor, temperature, water and urine state
oxygen/carbon-dioxide/vapor diffuse through connected non-solid cells; carbon dioxide has an authored downward density-bias transport
cave water and urine are separate liquid masses that fall under gravity and spread laterally through open cells
surface water can leak into open subsurface cells and surface urine can seep into caves or enrich moist soil
atmospheric vapor condenses into persistent cloud-water columns; wind advects cloud mass and cloud water precipitates into the surface water solver
living crawlers consume local oxygen, emit carbon dioxide, lose health/energy under oxygen depletion, accumulate bladder state and excrete urine into world state
the OffscreenCanvas environment worker renders cave voids, cave liquids, gas-dependent cave haze, clouds, surface water contamination and the existing organisms/plants
mobile telemetry exposes mean oxygen/carbon dioxide, cave-water mass, cloud water and selected-organism oxygen/bladder state
approximations: the cave atmosphere is a 2D cellular diffusion/transport approximation, not compressible gas CFD
water and urine in caves use gravity/lateral cellular transport rather than Navier-Stokes, SPH, FLIP or MPM
surface rivers/ocean still use the separate one-dimensional side-view shallow-water approximation
caves are cell-volume voids under the side-view terrain and are not full 3D geometry
carbon-dioxide sinking is an authored density-bias transport term rather than a full buoyant gas solver
clouds use vapor capacity, condensation, advection and precipitation columns rather than atmospheric CFD
urine is a separate contaminated-liquid scalar without detailed chemistry, microbes or solute reactions yet
the ALife controller remains authored drive arbitration with decaying memory and is not learning
creature articulation remains 2D Verlet/distance constraints with authored gait actuation

scratch_alife.note: ALife behavior proof from PR 93 remains valid for alife.js and also passed in the environment rerun.

failed_attempt.reason: test expected water to remain in the immediately lower cell after 50 steps; liquid had already fallen farther. Test was corrected to measure downward center-of-mass while conserving mass.

legacy_ecosystem_stack.note: Previous V100-V110 and patch layers remain in repository history/files but are not imported by the current route.

active_objective: Exercise the deployed cave/atmosphere/multi-fluid build on iPhone and judge cave readability, cloud motion, underground pooling, oxygen/CO2 behavior and contaminated-liquid flow.
next_gate: LIVE_TESTED and DEVICE_TESTED require actual deployed browser/iPhone execution after this environment change. CI_PASS alone is not sufficient.
invariants: Active route must not import archived V100-V110 layers
No third-party runtime libraries in the scratch engine
Rendering must run through transferred OffscreenCanvas in a worker
Do not call cellular gas transport CFD
Do not call cave liquids Navier-Stokes
Do not call the ALife controller learning
CI_PASS does not imply LIVE_TESTED or DEVICE_TESTED
